scope:
Execute archived domain-index and loader planning bodies on synthetic finite
CPU datasets. No JAX permutation, background worker, model loss or sharded arrays.
checks: Domain finite length equals concatenated child lengths
Domain offsets are stable cumulative boundaries
Boundary selects first item of next dataset
Original batch mapping restores unsorted duplicate indices
Tag vectors stay attached to the original item
Positive cap takes a prefix from each domain
Original planning restarts the default iterator from zero
Final partial batch retains all logical items exactly once
Exact-multiple stream yields two batches rather than len estimate
Original len overcounts exact-multiple progress estimate
Partial-length progress estimate matches three logical batches
Disabling partial padding drops the partial logical batch
Changing fetch grouping does not change logical stream
Explicit start from batch one omits only the first logical batch
Original __iter__ creates a new default-start iterator
Original timing wrapper immediately creates a new loader iterator
Hero builder omits shuffle and archived evaluator defaults false
Latest declared eval has no cap and batch 704
Latest eval uses explicit validation caches without train validation split
PTB and Twitter declarations keep fixed dated cache paths
Padding helper explicitly delegates to tree_zeros_like
